findings.title: forEach(async ...) does not await calendar/video deletions
findings.body: The code wraps the bookingRef iteration in `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })`. `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores the return value of its callback and does not await Promises, so the async callbacks (which now `await getCalendar(...)` and invoke `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` / `deleteMeeting(...)`) are fire-and-forget. The outer `Reschedule` function returns as soon as the synchronous work completes, before the calendar/video integrations have been cancelled. Previously these were synchronous calls; the async refactor turned them into background tasks. The booking row is updated to CANCELLED and `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` is awaited before these deletions actually run, which is a data-integrity regression (integrations can stay in sync with the old time slot after the DB has already been flipped). Replace the `forEach` with a sequential `for...of` (or `Promise.all(refs.map(...))`) so the deletions are awaited.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) does not await calendar/video deletions
findings.body: Identical antipattern to vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })`. After making the inner callback async, forEach no longer awaits any of the calendar `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` Promises. The `Reschedule` function continues running and the `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` is awaited before the integration deletions actually execute. Result: the booking is updated, the reschedule email goes out, and the function returns before the previous Google/Outlook/Zoom events are cancelled. Convert to a real awaited loop.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) drops recurring calendar deletion promises
forEach(async ...) skips calendar/video cancellations on reschedule
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` does not await the async callback. Inside, the code `await`s `getCalendar(...)` and calls `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` and `deleteMeeting(...)`, but because forEach discards the returned Promise and does not block, the `requestReschedule` mutation can finish — sending `sendRequestRescheduleEmail`, webhooks, and returning to the caller — before any of the previous calendar/video entries are cancelled. Previously these calls were synchronous; the async conversion silently turned them into best-effort background work. Replace with `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered) { ... }` or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))`.
